newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips mixed in heavy share trading.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips mixed in heavy share trading.

text.p: Nigerian blue chip stocks ended mixed on Monday in heavy turnover, traders said.
The all-share index rose to 6700.84 from Friday's 6698.79.
Traders said it was hard to predict the market as investors resumed selling blue chips while mopping up rising oil and brewing stocks.
Major conglomerate Lever Brothers started the week under pressure, forcing traders to price its shares 35 kobo down. It closed at 24.50 naira as investors took profit.
Nigerian-German Chemical Company was 30 kobo lower at 8.70 naira, the same as Guinness which went down to 5.95 naira.
Union Bank was down 20 kobo to 6.40 naira and packaging firm CMB, whose half-year result showed it was still in the red, slumped 17 kobo to 3.23 naira.
But big gains by Nigerian Breweries and the oil marketing companies ensured the index ended up.
The brewer was 40 kobo higher at 13.20 naira while National Oil peaked at 40.90 naira, up 30 kobo.
African Petroleum was 20 kobo more at 38.05 naira the same as Mobil which rose to 44.20 naira.
Nestle Foods was among gainers, rising 20 kobo at 42.20 naira while Flour Mills finished 10 kobo down at 10.70 naira.
West African Portland Cement was the sector's sole gainer at 38.50 naira, 20 kobo more.
